newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Afrox says trading to remain difficult.
newsitem.headline: Afrox says trading to remain difficult.

text.p: South African gases and healthcare group African Oxygen Ltd said on Thursday that trading conditions were expected to remain difficult in the second half of the year.
Afrox, which announced historic cost earnings per share of 33.1 cents against 31.4 in the half year to end-March, said its trading environment had slowed and become more competitive.
In addition, the company was hit by several one-off factors, said chairman Royden Vice.
"The half year was characterised by several non-recurring costs and product shortages which have now largely been solved," he said.

"Trading conditions for the last quarter of 1996 were very slow, affecting our performance for the full six months. Some improvement, however, was seen in the first quarter of this year and we expect this situation to continue for the remainder of our financial year."
One of the costs affecting results was a seven-week strike by some workers which cost over six million rand.
The company said it was continuing to invest in new plants which would enable continued growth.

The Mpumalanga gases project, Afrox's largest project to date, is on schedule for commissioning in July 1997 when it will supply oxygen, nitrogen and argon via a 50 km pipleine between Witbank and Middelburg.
